comments.comment: 0:28 "A black hole appears when an extraordinary amount of matter"  Nope. You dont need extraordinary amounts of matter to form a black hole. You simply need any amount X of matter compressed below its Schwarzchild radius.  0:48 "If you were to fall into a black hole nothing bad would happen until you crossed the event horizon" That depends on the mass of the black hole. That statement is true for supermassive black holes without accretion disks (if there was a disk, it would vaporize you well before you ever got close to the horizon). If the BH is small enough (< 30 solar masses), you will get spaghettified before reaching the event horizon. That is bad news for your survival. The smaller the BH, the faster you die before reaching the horizon.  Also this video is very simplified. If youre interested in getting to the hairy details, including hairy black holes (thats a real thing), you should check out PBS Spacetime and Sixty Symbol videos on BH's.
